messages.subject: Re: Activity data output
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lisa,

You can use "epochvalues2csv = TRUE" in your script to generate csv files containing epoch level data.
As long as you specified windowsizes = c(60,900,3600) then you would get 60s epoch files with a 15 min non-wear detection resolution and 60 min non-wear evaluation window

Kind regards,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: Activity data output
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lisa,

bodylocation simply generates the column in the summary files as a log to inform the user where the device was worn, and this only works if you actually specify this in the software when setting this up. If you don't specify the wear site you still get all the same data but bodylocation will state "not extracted" on each row.

You would need to read around the comparability of data when worn on chest vs wrist, and treat the output data accordingly - This won't be done in GGIR. I have only used accelerometers on thigh, wrist and waist so I'm afraid I can't really help, but someone else may chip in here if they know of any literature that might help guide your interpretation.

Kind regards,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Activity data output
messages.body_plain:
In addition to Ben's response it may be good to clarify that:

- Default sleep detection approach is optimized for wrist, possibly the algorithm also works for other body locations with some tweaking of parameters, but there is no literature yet on the validity of that.
- Time spent in inactivity, light, moderate or vigorous physical activity is done based on thresholds. The defaults are set for wrist, but you as user can modify them as you wish and tailor them to other attachment locations. I put some guidance here <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#published-cut-points-and-how-to-use-them>.
- All other output variables are basic descriptors of the data, and should be interpreted with the attachment location in mind.
- Non-wear detection should work across attachment locations, since not wearing an accelerometer is by definition not attachment specific.
- Auto-calibration success might be challenged, but part 2 csv report will always tell you whether it had difficulty reducing the calibration error. If it is a problem then you may want to consider doing separate calibration experiments and use the calibration correction coefficients from those as input (see documentation for backup.cal.coef)

Best,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant

messages.subject: Combining 2 half days' data as a single day of 24h?
messages.subject_clean: Combining 2 half days' data as a single day of 24h?
messages.body_plain:
Hi!
I'm processing AX3 data in cwa and participants from my sample wore the devices for 8 calendar days, for  example from Wednesday  starting at noon, until next Wed ending at noon.  The code runs well, but as expected, I get the day summary data of 8 days, where the first and the last days (both Wednesdays) have around 12 valid hours each, corresponding to after noon and before noon, respectively. I'd like to combine the 12-hours data corresponding to day 1 with the 12-hours data from day 8  as a single day,  to have a total of 7 full days with 24 hours. Any advice on how to do this with GGIR??
Thanks in advance!

messages.body_plain:
Hi to everyone,  I'm new to this group and an unexperienced user of R.

My aim is to analyze GENEActive Accelerometer data unsing GGIR. I have 10 7 days datasets which i want to analyze. I was able to run parts 1-5 and generate the reports.

Is it possible to generate the csv report from part 5 (part5_daysummary_WW_L30M100V400_T5A5) but for specific timewindows. My main interest lies in the variables dur_spt_wake_IN_min, dur_spt_wake_LIG_min, dur_spt_wake_MOD_min and dur_spt_wake_VIG_min.

Here an example:
Data file 1:  start: 24.11.2020 08:00:00 end: 03.12.2020 11:00:00

Timewindow 1: start: 24.11.2020 09:00:00 end: 25.12.2020 09:00:00
Timewindow 2: start: 01.12.2020 08:05:00 end: 02.12.2020 08:05:00

My idea was to use qwindow and a diary file with the timewindows im interested in. Unfortunately it did not work.

Since in the visual reports (attached Picture), show the different physical activity levels, i assume that it should be possible to get the time in the specific physical activity niveau.

Thanks for your help.

Greetings,
simon

messages.subject: Day sleep detection
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
First of all, thanks Vincent and others collaborators for all your work. I'm new at actigraphy field and I started to try some packages to use in my phD. Finally, I choose GGIR and I hope to learn and do future help in this work.

With this in mind, I ran a batch of raw GeneActiv files with this comand:

g.shell.GGIR(
     datadir="/Volumes/actigraphy/data/1479",
     outputdir="/Volumes/actigraphy",
     mode = c(1,2,3,4,5),
     do.visual=TRUE,
     viewingwindow = 1,
     visualreport = TRUE,
     epochvalues2csv = TRUE
     )

After, I took a look to the results, I got almost no detection (only 1 in 14) in day sleep. Is it normal? I attached the report. My GGIR version is 2.2 and R version is 3.6.2.

Thanks in Advance,
Francisco.

P.S.: I don't know if this information is relevant, but, In this folder (1479) of my example, I have 8 .bin files from the same person. In this file I have 30 consecutive days of use in 20Hz.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Combining 2 half days' data as a single day of 24h?
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Combining 2 half days' data as a single day of 24h?
messages.body_plain:
This is not possible, and to be honest I am also not sure you should be trying it.

The person level variables in the GGIR part 2 output that have fullRecording in their name use all the available data in the recording, including the first and last day. All other variables assume that you have enough data from a single day.

Usually studies who start- and end the recording in the middle of the day expect the participant to travel to a clinic on those days, which is an extra reason not to rely too heavily on those recording days.

Have you seen other accelerometer software including those first and last day?
Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Day sleep detection
messages.body_plain:
Hi Francisco,

Great to hear you were able to figure out how to run GGIR.

Are you referring to part 4 csv reports when you refer to "After, I took a look to the results, I got almost no detection (only 1 in 14) in day sleep"? Please note that the .pdf visualisation you attached is not supposed to show daytime 'sleep'.

GGIR produces estimates of daytime 'sustained inactivity bouts', which is a term I introduced to avoid having to call them naps. Calling it daytime sleep or daytime napping is tricky as there are no studies that have directly investigated the validity of this. I do not think the PSG night-time studies I did are sufficient to support the claim that nap detection is reliable. Further, short lasting non-wear periods (< 15 minutes) that are missed by the non-wear detection are likely to be labelled as sustained inactivity bout. So, I think it is best to interpret them or their absence carefully.

Whether it is plausible to not see sustained inactivity bout in your participants also depends on whether you expect them to take naps or to take off the sensor for short periods of time.

Cheers,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Good point Marcus. The exported time series indeed give you endless freedom to analyse the data as you wish. However, if it turns out that many GGIR users want this functionality then it may be worth adding it as a standard functionality to safe everyone the time of developing their own scripts.

One of the challenges I imagine is to account for the irregular availability of specific hours in the day, e.g. one one day 10-11am may be available as daytime waking hour while on another day the person may still be asleep.
Cheers,
Vincent
